lines.text: The motor runs its own control loop. Tuner X just sends it a target, and draws what happens.
Start with every gain at zero, and enable. Nothing moves. That's correct: zero gains mean zero volts.
Gravity pulls hardest when the arm is level, and not at all when it's straight up.
The gravity gain cancels exactly that pull, at every angle. Raise it until the arm holds level on its own.
The static gain covers friction. Set it to half the gap between the smallest and largest gravity gains that hold.
Now the feedback. Double the proportional gain until the arm overshoots, then cut it in half.
The derivative gain takes out the overshoot. Too much of it, and the arm buzzes.
Try it. Pick a gain that's too low, then one that's too high, and watch the plot.
Three shapes tell you what's wrong. It runs away, it buzzes, or it falls short. Read the plot, not the mechanism.
Apply the gains, and power cycle. They're saved on the motor.
Feedforward pays for holding. Feedback fixes what's left. A tuned arm makes one motion, and then it's silent.
